::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 23d [1868]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 212-3
:::

My dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
The mistakes about Walsingham & Sidney had perhaps better be mentioned in the preface to disarm the critics, and that unlucky Amen must be made an erratum it is so ridiculous in its present position.[^1]

Would you notify this to [Clay](organizations/other_173.qmd), as I do not know the page.

What do you say to the [story of Indian Life](organizations/other_202.qmd) I sent you? If you cannot do any thing with it, please write to me before returning it, for I think I shall ask [Mr Warne](people/person_1433.qmd) to look at it, and it is a pity it should travel 140 miles between Nos 15 and 16[^2]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Endorsed ‘Routledge attending to this’.  These anachronisms were noted in the preface to *The Chaplet of Pearls*.
[^2]: Frederick Warne (1825-1901), publisher, had offices at 15 Bedford Street, next door to Macmillan.
